opening.argument: Judge, the question in the title matters: the creator presents these programs as something to examine, not as settled safe investments. He says he will leave material for viewers to research and intends to research the programs further himself. Those qualifications do not erase the referral link, but they weaken the claim that he is asking viewers to accept an assured income opportunity on his authority.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a referral link and an invitation to build a network, but neither quoted statement promises a return or tells viewers that recruiting will reliably pay them. The speaker also explicitly sends viewers to do their own research. A displayed account can show how a program works without establishing that the speaker guarantees its rewards.

That sequence supports reading the video as a demonstration of interfaces and setup steps, rather than a demand that viewers join a particular income scheme.

opening.argument: Judge, the observable pitch can be read as a service's free-coin and referral promotion. The speaker calls CoinPro a P2P payment system, describes daily coins and unlocks, and points to a referral link. Those facts alone do not show a required deposit, a promised fixed return, or a viewer being asked to hand over credentials. Even the displayed referral features do not, by themselves, prove that a viewer must recruit anyone to use the payment service.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the referral screen and invitation go beyond a bare discount code. But its evidence still leaves open whether the displayed percentages are guaranteed income, whether payment is required to participate, or whether every user must build a downline. The speaker's description of a payment system with daily coins permits an ordinary rewards reading of the material actually shown.
